plain.body: Before RSI-006, the productivity question — does a governed recursive improvement actually produce more verified progress per dollar? — was already asked once, on live infrastructure. The answer was negative evidence, preserved, not hidden.
plain.headline: The earlier productivity attempt did not produce the claim.

records.plain: Preregistered acceptance rules: minimum raw success-rate advantage 0.05, minimum success-per-dollar ratio 1.2, at least one recursive promotion with subsequent live use, per-arm spend ceiling $2.25. Cost accounting by pinned-Hermes telemetry only — no imputation, no reconstruction.

Formal verdict: INCONCLUSIVE_RIL_001R_LIVE_EXECUTION — the receiver compared numeric limit values by string representation (worker emitted 0.50, receiver expected Decimal string 0.5). Terminal: 24/24 control, 24/24 recursive; control $0.88007, recursive $0.89462; success-per-dollar ratio 0.9837, below the preregistered 1.2 threshold. Scientific interpretation: recursive_advantage NOT_ESTABLISHED.

weaknesses: Raw result bytes are not in the frozen local record. The full RIL_001R_RESULT.json lives in a GitHub Actions artifact; only its SHA-256 is quoted locally. This replay shows the freeze record's terminal numbers — inspectable at the artifact link, not reconstructed here.

Both arms saturated the 24-case arena at 24/24, so the ratio was measured where neither arm could show an advantage. Present as “no advantage observed on a saturated arena”, never as “the recursive arm lost”.
The formal verdict is INCONCLUSIVE on a measurement defect. The negative finding is preserved separately from the verdict.
lanes.why_it_matters: This lane is the history that the future RSI-006 productivity slot plugs into. RSI-006 is the next attempt at this question — not the first. Nothing here is replaced when RSI-006 earns its result; the lane grows.
